findings.issue: Fenced-content skipping is asymmetric: section state and BlockingFindingIDs are guarded by !inFence, but the FindingIDs scrape is not, so ids quoted in a fenced block still land in FindingIDs.
findings.consequence: A fenced/quoted id the ledger holds as an open blocking-class row keeps the log a gate input after its declared blockers resolve — fail-closed (stays blocking), not fail-open.

findings.issue: The fence toggle matches any 3-backtick line and ignores fence length, so a 4-backtick fence containing an inner ``` would toggle inFence off mid-block.
findings.consequence: Reachability is limited (no committed review log uses a 4-backtick fence; context packs are not parsed by Discover), so a latent gap rather than a live mis-parse.

findings.issue: The !inFence guard on the section-state switch and on the header boundary is not isolated by any fixture.
findings.consequence: A fenced non-mrvf level-2/3 heading closing the section (or opening it first) is untested, so removing the guard passes the suite.

findings.issue: The 'vouched == 0' guard in LogBlockersResolvedInLedger is not isolated — every case sets BlockingFindingCount >= 1, so the count tripwire fires first.
findings.consequence: The guard only bites when BlockingFindingCount==0 with an advisory-only blocking section; that input has no test, so deleting the guard passes CI.

verdict.reasoning: The asymmetry is intentional in the diff: FindingIDs remains the broad inventory of every referenced ID, while BlockingFindingIDs records only declared blocker headings outside fences. The claimed gating consequence depends on downstream code treating FindingIDs as blockers, but no such code or evidence is provided here; the added comments instead state that the gate distinguishes BlockingFindingIDs. Thus the alleged fail-closed behavior is not verifiable from this diff.

The parser toggles inFence for every trimmed line beginning with three backticks, without recording the opening fence length. Thus a four-backtick fence opens the block, but an embedded three-backtick line incorrectly closes it, allowing subsequent headings and finding IDs inside the literal block to affect parsing. This violates the stated fenced-code invariant even if current logs do not exercise it.

The added fixture contains a fenced `## Example`, but it appears only after the declared blocker has already been collected and before a real `## Advisory Findings` heading. If the `!inFence` guard on section switching were removed, that fenced heading would prematurely close the blocking section without changing either asserted result. Likewise, the header boundary is already closed by `## Verdict`, so that guard is not pinned there either. The tests in view therefore exercise fenced text but do not make these guards observable, allowing the claimed invariant to be removed while the assertions still pass.

The shown tests do not isolate `vouched == 0`, but the relevant `projector_test.go` hunk is explicitly incomplete and ends mid-test. The omitted added lines could include the advisory-only, `BlockingFindingCount == 0` case. Therefore the evidence is insufficient to verify the claim that deleting the guard passes CI.
